dialog.body: Recreation department, this is Beth. Good morning, how can I help you?

Yes, hello, good morning. Um, I'm calling about the classes, the recreation classes. For the winter, I think. I saw something on the, the flyer, and I want to make sure I'm calling the right place. Is this the right place?
You've got the right place. Which class were you interested in?

Well, it's not for me, it's for my grandson, no, wait, my neighbor's boy. No. Let me start over. I'm Andres Quintero. There's a boy on my street, his mother asked me to ask, because I'm the one who is home, and she works days. She wants to know about the scholarship. For the class fees. Is there a scholarship? Is that a real thing?

Yes, there's a scholarship program for class fees, so families who can't cover the full cost can apply for help. It's a short form, and you or his mom can pick it up at the office or we can send it along.
A form. Okay. Is it okay if I get the form and not her? Because I don't want to do it wrong. I don't want it to be a problem that it's me and not the mother.
You can pick up the blank form, no problem at all. She'd need to fill it out and sign it herself, though, since she's the parent.

Right, right, she signs. I just bring it. That's okay then. I just bring it to her and she signs it. Good. And then, um, how does it work, is the money taken off the class or does she pay and get it back?
It's taken off the class fee. Once it's approved, she'd pay whatever the remaining part is, if there is any, and that's it. Nobody pays first and waits for money back.
Okay. Okay. So not pay first. That's what I wanted to be sure of. Because she said maybe you pay and then they pay you back, and I said I don't think so, but I wasn't sure.
No, it comes off up front. You were right.

Good. Now, the age. Is there an age limit? The boy is nine. Is nine okay? Is he too young, or too old? I don't know how they divide them. Some are for the little ones and some are for teenagers, so is nine okay?
Nine is a great age. Most of our youth classes run something like six to twelve, and then there are separate teen ones. Which class was it on the flyer?
Oh. The flyer. I don't have it in front of me. It was, um, it had a picture of a basketball. Or a ball, maybe a kickball. Is that one okay for nine?

If it's the youth basketball, nine should be fine. If you can find the flyer or just tell his mom to look at the age range printed on it, that'll confirm it. Or call me back with the name of it and I'll check.

Yes, I'll look. I'll look for it. She might have it on the, the refrigerator. Everybody on the street has everything on the refrigerator. And the group text, there's a group text chain on our street and it never stops, never. Forty messages about the plow, and the rain, and who has the trash can. That's how she heard about the classes, somebody put it in the chain.
Well, that's one way word gets around. Did the storm last weekend give your street any trouble?

Oh, the snow and the rain, Sunday into Monday. No, it was fine, it was just slushy. I just want to be sure about the form. So I come and pick up the form, she signs, and the age is okay. Is that right? That's everything?
That's it. Come by during office hours and ask for the scholarship application. If you tell me the class once you find the flyer, I can also note it so it's ready for you.
Okay. And is it okay if I come today? Or is it better tomorrow? I don't want to come at a bad time.
Today's fine. We're here until the afternoon, so you've got time. Just come to the front desk.
Good. Thank you. I'm sorry, I asked it a few times. I just want it done right for the boy.
Don't apologize, that's what I'm here for. We'll see you soon, Mr. Quintero.
Thank you, thank you. Goodbye.
